cards.subject: Least privilege
says: gives each person only the access their job needs
limits the damage a mistaken or compromised account can do
is checked against what a person actually does, not their seniority
cards.use: need to decide how much access a new starter should get
not: grants everyone full access to save setup time

cards.subject: Role-based access control
says: bundles permissions into named roles that people are assigned
lets access change by moving a person between roles
avoids granting each permission to each person one by one
cards.use: want access to follow job titles rather than individual requests
not: assigns every permission directly to a named person

cards.subject: Separation of duties
says: splits a risky task so no single person can complete it alone
makes the person who requests an action differ from the one who approves it
reduces the chance of undetected error or fraud
cards.use: must stop one person from both raising and approving a payment
not: lets the author of a change approve it without another person

cards.subject: Access review
says: compares who holds access with who should hold it
finds access left behind after a person changes role
is repeated on a regular schedule rather than done once
cards.use: suspect people kept permissions from earlier jobs
not: happens only once, when the account is first created

cards.subject: Joiner-mover-leaver process
says: covers access changes when people join, change role or leave
treats a role change as an access event, not only a hire or exit
keeps access aligned with the person's current job
cards.use: want one routine that handles starters, transfers and departures
not: applies only on the day a person is hired

cards.subject: Privileged access
says: allows actions that can change other people's access or critical settings
is held by few people and for a limited time
needs stronger approval and logging than ordinary access
cards.use: must decide who can change other users' roles
not: is given to all staff by default

cards.subject: Shared account
says: lets several people sign in with one set of credentials
makes it impossible to tell which person did an action
must have its password changed when any user leaves
cards.use: find that one login is used by a whole team
not: records exactly which individual performed each action

cards.subject: Break-glass access
says: gives emergency access outside normal approval for a defined crisis
is logged and reviewed afterwards
is held sealed and used only when ordinary routes fail
cards.use: need an emergency route when the usual approver is unreachable
not: replaces normal access for everyday work

cards.subject: Permission creep
says: builds up as people collect access across successive roles
leaves a person with more rights than their current job needs
is found by comparing current access to current duties
cards.use: notice a long-serving employee can reach systems unrelated to their job
not: happens only when an account is hacked

cards.subject: Service account
says: lets software rather than a person sign in to a system
has no human owner who can answer a security challenge
needs a named person responsible for it and for rotating its secrets
cards.use: need an automated job to reach a system without a person logging in
not: is safe to share among all engineers

cards.subject: Pre-boarding
says: prepares accounts, equipment and a welcome before the first day
reduces idle time and anxiety at the start
begins once an offer is accepted
cards.use: want a new starter productive on day one
not: starts only at the end of the first month

cards.subject: Onboarding checklist
says: lists the access, learning and introductions a new person needs
makes starts consistent from one hire to the next
gives the manager a record of what has been done
cards.use: want every new hire to get the same complete start
not: is written fresh from memory for each hire

cards.subject: Buddy
says: is a peer named to help a new person with everyday questions
is separate from the line manager
helps the newcomer learn unwritten norms
cards.use: want a new starter to have a safe person to ask small questions
not: decides the new person's pay and promotion

cards.subject: First-week plan
says: sets out the specific meetings, tools and tasks for the opening days
includes introductions to the people the newcomer will work with
gives a first small real task to build confidence
cards.use: need to schedule the opening days of a new hire
not: is a long-term career plan

cards.subject: 30-60-90 day plan
says: divides the first three months into learning, contributing and owning phases
sets expectations that a manager and new hire agree together
gives natural points for progress conversations
cards.use: want clear milestones for a new person's first quarter
not: covers only the first three days

cards.subject: Role-based learning path
says: assigns study material according to a person's job role
puts the most essential topics first
saves each person from choosing what to learn from scratch
cards.use: want new hires in the same job to learn the same core things
not: gives every employee the identical syllabus regardless of job

cards.subject: Shadowing
says: has a newcomer watch an experienced person do real work
shows how tasks are done in practice beyond the documents
is followed by the newcomer doing the task with support
cards.use: want a new starter to see a task done before attempting it
not: means the newcomer works alone from day one

cards.subject: Orientation
says: introduces the organisation, its policies and its facilities
is usually a short one-off event
covers the basics every employee needs
cards.use: need to give new people the company-wide basics
not: is the whole of a new hire's role training

cards.subject: Onboarding feedback survey
says: asks new hires what helped and what was missing
improves the process for the next cohort
is most useful when sent after a few weeks, not on day one
cards.use: want evidence on how well starts are going
not: measures how long people stay in the job

cards.subject: Time to productivity
says: measures how long a new hire takes to work at the expected level
varies by role and complexity of the job
is shortened by clear goals and early real tasks
cards.use: want to judge whether onboarding is effective
not: counts only the hours spent in training

cards.subject: Access revocation
says: removes accounts and permissions when employment ends
happens across every system, not only the main one
should take effect at the moment employment ends
cards.use: need to stop a departed person reaching company systems
not: can wait a few weeks after the person leaves

cards.subject: Session invalidation
says: signs out logins that are already open
closes the gap left when only the account is disabled
stops a stale token from continuing to work
cards.use: worry that a leaver's open sessions stay usable after disabling
not: only hides the account from the directory

cards.subject: Knowledge handover
says: transfers what a leaver knew to the people who stay
covers processes that exist only in one person's head
starts before the last day
cards.use: fear a process will be lost when its owner leaves
not: is optional once the person has left

cards.subject: Handover notes
says: record what a person owns, how it works and what is pending
are written for a named successor to read
list contacts, schedules and known problems
cards.use: need a written record of an area before its owner leaves
not: are the exit interview transcript

cards.subject: Exit interview
says: collects the leaver's honest view on why they are going
gives themes about management, pay and workload
is a source of improvement ideas, not of handover detail
cards.use: want to learn why people leave
not: transfers ownership of accounts and files

cards.subject: Ownership transfer
says: moves accounts, files, customers and tasks to a named person
prevents orphaned work with no owner
is confirmed by the receiver, not assumed
cards.use: find that a leaver owned customer accounts and shared files
not: deletes the leaver's files

cards.subject: Secret rotation
says: changes passwords and keys a leaver knew
closes routes that work independently of the person's own account
applies especially to shared credentials
cards.use: know that a leaver had a shared password or API key
not: is unnecessary once the login is disabled

cards.subject: Equipment return
says: recovers laptops, devices and badges
is recorded so nothing is left unaccounted for
pairs with wiping or reassigning the device
cards.use: need to collect company hardware from a leaver
not: covers only the leaver's paper files

cards.subject: Two-person offboarding
says: has a second person check the steps for privileged leavers
catches steps missed by the first person
is a form of separation of duties applied to exits
cards.use: are removing someone who held broad privileged access
not: lets one person sign off their own checklist alone

cards.subject: Soft removal
says: marks a person as left instead of deleting their record
keeps history and references intact
prevents sign-in while preserving who did what
cards.use: must keep audit history but stop a person from logging in
not: erases every trace of the person from the system

cards.subject: Probation period
says: is an initial period in which fit for the job is assessed
has set objectives and review points
ends with a confirm, extend or end decision
cards.use: are starting a new hire and want a structured assessment window
not: guarantees the job for life

cards.subject: Probation objectives
says: state what the new hire must show by the end of the period
are agreed in writing at the start
are specific enough to judge as met or not met
cards.use: want a new hire to know what success looks like
not: are drawn up only at the final review

cards.subject: Probation review
says: compares progress with the agreed objectives at a set point
gives the person feedback with time left to improve
is recorded so the later decision has evidence
cards.use: are reaching a scheduled progress point in someone's first months
not: happens only when someone resigns

cards.subject: Mid-point check-in
says: happens halfway through the period to flag concerns early
gives the person time to change course
avoids a surprise at the final decision
cards.use: want to raise a concern while there is still time to fix it
not: replaces the final probation review

cards.subject: Probation extension
says: lengthens the period when evidence is not yet enough to decide
comes with clear new objectives and a new date
should be explained to the person in writing
cards.use: cannot yet tell if a new hire meets the standard
not: is a silent way to avoid a hard decision

cards.subject: Probation confirmation
says: confirms a new hire has met the objectives and continues in the role
is communicated in writing
moves the person to the normal performance cycle
cards.use: have reached the end of probation with objectives met
not: is automatic with no decision recorded

cards.subject: Early warning conversation
says: tells a struggling new hire where they fall short and what to change
is held as soon as the gap is seen
avoids a surprise when a decision is taken
cards.use: notice a new hire missing the standard in the first weeks
not: is saved for the last day of the period

cards.subject: Support plan
says: pairs named help such as coaching or training with the objectives
tests whether a gap is skill, clarity or environment
is offered before a negative decision
cards.use: suspect a new hire's difficulty comes from missing support
not: is a penalty given to the person

cards.subject: Goal setting
says: agrees what a person is expected to achieve in a period
links individual work to team and company aims
is revisited as priorities change
cards.use: need to make clear what good looks like for the next quarter
not: happens only at the end of the year

cards.subject: SMART goal
says: is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound
can be judged as met or not at a date
avoids vague aims such as work harder
cards.use: need a goal that can be checked at its deadline
not: is defined by being as ambitious as possible

cards.subject: Objectives and key results
says: pairs an inspiring objective with measurable key results
is usually set for a quarter or a year
can be used to stretch rather than only to check
cards.use: want ambitious aims with measurable results attached
not: is a pay scale

cards.subject: Continuous feedback
says: gives people input close to the event it concerns
makes the formal review contain no surprises
works in both directions between people and managers
cards.use: want feedback to be useful at the time it happens
not: is saved up for the annual review

cards.subject: Situation-behaviour-impact feedback
says: describes the situation, the observed behaviour and its effect
keeps feedback on actions rather than personality
gives the person facts they can act on
cards.use: need a structure for specific, non-judgemental feedback
not: begins by judging the person's character

cards.subject: Performance review
says: assesses performance across a set period against expectations
produces a written record agreed with the person
feeds into development and, in many places, pay decisions
cards.use: are reaching the formal assessment point in the cycle
not: is the only time feedback is ever given

cards.subject: Calibration
says: compares ratings across managers to keep standards consistent
reduces differences caused by lenient or harsh raters
is a discussion of evidence, not a vote on people
cards.use: worry that two managers rate the same work differently
not: lets each manager set their own private scale

cards.subject: Self-assessment
says: asks a person to assess their own work before the review
brings the person's view and evidence into the conversation
exposes differences between self-view and manager view
cards.use: want the person's own account before the manager forms a view
not: replaces the manager's assessment

cards.subject: 360 feedback
says: collects views from peers, reports, managers and sometimes others
shows how behaviour is seen from several directions
is best used for development rather than a single rating
cards.use: want a rounded picture of how someone works with others
not: comes only from the person's line manager

cards.subject: Performance improvement plan
says: sets specific expectations, support and a review date for a gap
is a documented and time-limited process
should follow earlier feedback, not be the first the person hears
cards.use: have a sustained gap that earlier feedback has not closed
not: is a surprise given with no earlier warning

cards.subject: Recency bias
says: gives too much weight to the latest events in a period
is reduced by keeping notes through the whole period
makes a review reflect weeks rather than the year
cards.use: notice a review mentions only the last month
not: favours the earliest event in a period

cards.subject: Halo effect
says: lets one strong trait colour judgement of everything else
can make a likeable person look better at the whole job
is reduced by scoring each criterion separately
cards.use: see a person rated highly on all criteria because of one strength
not: gives too much weight to recent events

cards.subject: Annual leave
says: is paid time off taken for rest
is requested in advance and approved against team cover
accrues or is allocated according to the employer's policy
cards.use: want planned time off for a holiday
not: is time off only for illness

cards.subject: Sick leave
says: covers absence because of illness or injury
is reported on the day, following the reporting procedure
is not normally scheduled in advance
cards.use: are unwell and cannot work today
not: is booked weeks ahead like a holiday

cards.subject: Parental leave
says: is time away from work around the arrival of a child
is planned with notice so work can be covered
ends with a return conversation and handover back
cards.use: need to plan cover for a long, planned absence of a team member
not: is unplanned time off at a few hours' notice

cards.subject: Leave balance
says: records how much leave a person has accrued, taken and left
is checked before a request is approved
is carried forward or lapses under the written policy
cards.use: need to know how many days a person can still take
not: is the number of people absent today

cards.subject: Leave approval workflow
says: routes a request to the manager who knows the team's cover
records the decision so both sides have evidence
is checked against clashes with other absences
cards.use: need to decide whether two people can be away at once
not: approves every request automatically with no check

cards.subject: Cover plan
says: names who handles a person's work while they are away
is agreed before the absence starts
lists urgent items and who decides in the person's place
cards.use: must keep work moving while a person is absent
not: is written after the person returns

cards.subject: Handover before leave
says: gives the cover person the context, pending items and contacts
reduces calls to someone who is meant to be away
is written down, not only said in passing
cards.use: are about to go on leave with live work in progress
not: means the person stays reachable throughout the leave

cards.subject: Return-to-work conversation
says: welcomes a person back and catches up on what changed
checks whether any adjustments or support are needed
is held after sickness or long absences
cards.use: have a colleague returning after a long absence
not: is a disciplinary hearing

cards.subject: Unplanned absence procedure
says: tells staff whom to notify and by when if they cannot work
lets the manager trigger cover quickly
is known to everyone in advance
cards.use: need staff to know what to do when they cannot come in
not: is made up on the day it is first needed

cards.subject: Public holiday calendar
says: lists the days the organisation is closed for shared holidays
lets teams plan coverage around them
can differ between locations
cards.use: are planning rotas across offices in different places
not: is the same for every team in every location

cards.subject: Job description
says: states the purpose, duties and requirements of a role
is the base from which a vacancy is advertised
should be updated when the role changes
cards.use: need to explain what a vacancy involves
not: is a record of a person's past performance

cards.subject: Role scorecard
says: defines the outcomes and competencies a hire must show
is agreed before interviews begin
lets interviewers rate candidates on the same criteria
cards.use: want interviewers to judge candidates against the same standard
not: is written after the final choice is made

cards.subject: Structured interview
says: asks every candidate the same questions in the same order
scores answers against agreed criteria
predicts job performance better than free conversation
cards.use: want comparable, fair evidence across candidates
not: lets each interviewer improvise unrelated questions

cards.subject: Work sample
says: asks the candidate to do a small piece of real job work
shows skill directly instead of describing it
should be limited in time and fair to all candidates
cards.use: want to see how a candidate actually performs the work
not: is a personality questionnaire

cards.subject: Reference check
says: asks former colleagues to confirm a candidate's claims and work
is done with the candidate's permission
adds evidence from people who have seen the work
cards.use: want an outside view of a candidate before an offer
not: replaces the interview

cards.subject: Hiring pipeline
says: tracks candidates through stages from application to offer
shows where candidates are lost or delayed
gives each stage a named owner
cards.use: want to see how many candidates are at each stage
not: is a list of current employees

cards.subject: Candidate experience
says: is how the process feels to an applicant at every step
includes clear communication and timely replies
shapes whether a candidate accepts or recommends the employer
cards.use: want rejected applicants to leave with a respectful impression
not: is measured only by offers accepted

cards.subject: Offer stage
says: makes a written proposal of the role and terms to the chosen candidate
follows the decision and approvals
ends with acceptance, negotiation or decline
cards.use: have chosen a candidate and must make it formal
not: is the first screening of applications

cards.subject: Interview debrief
says: gathers interviewers' independent scores before discussion
stops the loudest voice from setting the outcome
ends with a recorded decision and reasons
cards.use: want a hiring decision based on separate, written evidence
not: happens in the corridor with no notes

cards.subject: Unconscious bias in hiring
says: leads to favouring candidates who resemble the interviewer
is reduced by structure, scorecards and independent scoring
affects judgement even when people intend to be fair
cards.use: suspect decisions follow personal similarity rather than evidence
not: is removed by trusting first impressions

cards.subject: Interview panel
says: brings several interviewers who cover different criteria
avoids repeated questions across rounds
lets views be compared across independent raters
cards.use: need broader evidence than one interviewer provides
not: is one manager making all decisions alone

cards.subject: Daily stand-up
says: is a short daily meeting where a team shares progress and blockers
stays brief and focuses on coordination
is held at a fixed time
cards.use: need the team to surface blockers each day
not: is a long problem-solving session

cards.subject: Weekly team meeting
says: reviews priorities, news and upcoming work each week
keeps everyone aware of what others are doing
has an agenda circulated in advance
cards.use: want a regular time to align the whole team
not: replaces all one-to-one conversations

cards.subject: One-to-one meeting
says: is a regular private conversation between a manager and a report
belongs to the report and covers their concerns and growth
is not cancelled casually
cards.use: want a regular place for feedback, support and career talk
not: is a status report to the whole team

cards.subject: Retrospective
says: looks back at how the team worked and picks improvements
ends with a few agreed actions with owners
is held at the end of a cycle of work
cards.use: want the team to learn from the last period
not: is a forward plan of the next release

cards.subject: Planning meeting
says: decides what the team will take on in the coming period
sizes work against available capacity
accounts for planned leave and cover
cards.use: need to choose work for the next cycle
not: reviews what went wrong last time

cards.subject: All-hands
says: gathers the whole organisation for company news and direction
gives leaders a place to answer questions openly
is held less often than team meetings
cards.use: want to share company-wide updates with everyone
not: is a private meeting for managers only

cards.subject: Demo
says: shows finished work to people outside the team who care about it
gets feedback while change is still cheap
builds shared understanding of progress
cards.use: want stakeholders to see real results, not slides
not: is a closed meeting for the author only

cards.subject: Team charter
says: records the purpose, norms and ways of working a team agrees
is written together and revisited
helps new members learn how the team operates
cards.use: want a shared written agreement on how the team works
not: is a list of individual salaries

cards.subject: Working agreement
says: sets concrete rules such as response times and meeting hours
is short and agreed by everyone affected
is amended by the team when a rule on hours or response times stops helping
cards.use: need explicit expectations on availability and handoffs
not: is imposed by outside auditors

cards.subject: Decision log
says: records what was decided, by whom, when and why
lets later readers see the reasoning behind choices
prevents the same debate being reopened without new facts
cards.use: want to know why a past choice was made
not: is a to-do list of unfinished tasks

cards.subject: Career ladder
says: describes the levels of a job family and what each expects
shows people how to progress
makes expectations visible instead of implied
cards.use: want staff to see the path from one level to the next
not: is a list of open vacancies

cards.subject: Competency matrix
says: lists skills and behaviours expected at each level
lets a person compare their work to the next level
uses observable descriptions rather than adjectives
cards.use: need clear evidence for what each level requires
not: is a seating chart

cards.subject: Level
says: marks the scope and independence expected of a person
can differ from job title
sets the starting point for what a person may be trusted with
cards.use: need to know how much independence a person should have
not: is the same as years of service

cards.subject: Promotion
says: moves a person up a level after sustained work at that level
is based on evidence of the next level's expectations
comes with expanded scope
cards.use: have a person who has consistently performed at the next level
not: is a reward for long service alone

cards.subject: Individual contributor track
says: lets people progress in craft without managing others
has senior levels with wider technical or professional influence
avoids forcing good practitioners into management
cards.use: want to grow a skilled specialist who does not want to manage
not: requires managing a large team to progress

cards.subject: Management track
says: advances people who lead teams and outcomes
values coaching, planning and hiring skills
is a different job, not a reward for a strong specialist
cards.use: want to develop someone into a people leader
not: is the only way to earn a pay rise

cards.subject: Promotion packet
says: collects evidence of a person's work against the next level
is reviewed by people beyond the line manager
reduces dependence on one manager's opinion
cards.use: must support a promotion case with written evidence
not: is a letter of recommendation only

cards.subject: Mentor
says: offers advice from experience outside the line management chain
helps the mentee with career and judgement
is chosen for what they can teach, not for authority
cards.use: want career advice from a more experienced person who is not your manager
not: approves the mentee's pay and promotion

cards.subject: Sponsor
says: uses their influence to put a person forward for opportunities
speaks for the person in rooms the person is not in
is more active than a mentor
cards.use: want a senior person to advocate for a promising colleague
not: only gives advice and never acts on the person's behalf

cards.subject: Succession plan
says: names people who could take over critical roles
identifies the development each successor needs
reduces risk when a key person leaves
cards.use: worry about who could take over if a key person left suddenly
not: chooses a replacement only after someone resigns

cards.subject: Data minimisation
says: collects only the personal data needed for a purpose
reduces what can be lost or misused
asks for a reason before adding a new field
cards.use: are designing a form that asks about employees
not: collects everything in case it is useful later

cards.subject: Need-to-know
says: limits information to people whose work requires it
applies strongly to pay, health and disciplinary records
is the information version of least privilege
cards.use: must decide who may see a colleague's salary
not: shares sensitive details with the whole team

cards.subject: Personnel file
says: holds the formal records of one person's employment
has restricted access and a retention period
should contain facts, not casual opinions
cards.use: need to know where a person's contract and reviews are kept
not: is open for any employee to browse

cards.subject: Retention schedule
says: sets how long each kind of record is kept
triggers secure deletion when the period ends
avoids both premature loss and indefinite hoarding
cards.use: must decide when to delete old employee records
not: keeps everything forever by default

cards.subject: Sensitive personal data
says: covers details such as health, finances or protected characteristics
deserves tighter access and handling than ordinary contact data
should be collected only where truly necessary
cards.use: hold a document that discloses a person's medical condition
not: is the same as a work email address

cards.subject: Access logging
says: records who viewed or changed personal records and when
lets misuse be detected and investigated
depends on individual rather than shared accounts
cards.use: want to find out who opened a record
not: stores the contents of every record again

cards.subject: Redaction
says: removes or masks details before a document is shared
lets a record be used without revealing who it concerns
must be applied to the stored copy, not just hidden on screen
cards.use: must share an example case without naming the people involved
not: deletes the original record

cards.subject: Confidential review feedback
says: keeps individual peer comments away from the person reviewed unless agreed otherwise
encourages honest input
is shared as themes rather than attributed quotes
cards.use: collect peer comments for a colleague's review
not: is posted on a public channel

cards.subject: Secure sharing of staff data
says: sends staff records through approved channels with limited access
expires or revokes links once the need ends
avoids copies in personal email or chat
cards.use: must send payroll details to an external adviser
not: is done by attaching the file to a group email

cards.subject: Desk
says: is a named operating function that owns a queue and a set of duties
survives whoever sits at it
is what work and capabilities are granted to
cards.use: want a job to exist independently of one person
not: is a physical table in an office

cards.subject: Queue
says: holds the work items waiting for a desk to handle
makes the volume of waiting work visible
is owned by a named function
cards.use: need a single place where incoming work waits
not: is a list of staff holidays

cards.subject: Duty
says: is one bounded task a desk is responsible for
carries a class, a floor level and risk tags
can be assigned, trained and covered
cards.use: must break a role into definite responsibilities
not: is a general aspiration with no limits

cards.subject: Rota
says: shares a recurring responsibility among people on a schedule
makes cover predictable
spreads out-of-hours burden fairly
cards.use: need several people to take turns covering a service
not: fixes one person to the work permanently

cards.subject: Escalation path
says: names who takes an item the first handler cannot resolve
is defined before it is needed
stops items bouncing between people with no owner
cards.use: face a case the first-line handler cannot decide
not: sends the problem back to the customer

cards.subject: Runbook
says: gives step-by-step instructions for a recurring or urgent task
lets a trained stand-in act without the usual expert
is kept current by the people who use it
cards.use: want someone other than the expert to handle an incident
not: explains the company's history

cards.subject: Bus factor
says: counts how many people could leave before work stops
is low when only one person holds the knowledge
is raised by documenting and cross-training
cards.use: want to know how risky it is that one person knows a process
not: counts how many people sit in a team

cards.subject: Single point of failure
says: is one person or component whose loss stops the whole process
is removed by cover, backups and documentation
appears in people processes as well as systems
cards.use: find a process that only one person can run
not: is guaranteed to fail every time it is used

cards.subject: gglearn role set
says: has exactly three roles: learner, manager and admin
gives managers the running of people and content areas
gives admins the ability to do everything
cards.use: need to know what roles gglearn defines
not: has a separate payouts-clerk role

cards.subject: gglearn fresh authorization check
says: re-reads a person's role from the database on every request
makes a role change or offboarding take effect immediately
avoids waiting for a cookie to expire
cards.use: want a removed person to lose access at once in gglearn
not: trusts the role stored in the cookie until it expires

cards.subject: gglearn manager offboarding rule
says: lets managers offboard only learners
reserves offboarding of other people for admins
was added after a review found a manager could lock an admin out
cards.use: ask who a gglearn manager may offboard
not: lets a manager offboard an admin

cards.subject: gglearn self-offboarding block
says: stops anyone from offboarding their own account
applies even to admins
prevents accidental self-lockout
cards.use: want to know if an admin can offboard themselves in gglearn
not: lets admins offboard themselves freely

cards.subject: gglearn session version
says: is bumped on offboarding to sign out every existing session
lets old sessions be refused without waiting for them to expire
is stored against the user
cards.use: need gglearn to end all of a person's open sessions at once
not: is a counter of pages a user has visited

cards.subject: gglearn offboarded status
says: marks a user as offboarded instead of deleting the record
keeps history and references intact
blocks sign-in
cards.use: ask why gglearn keeps an offboarded person's row
not: removes the person's row from the database

cards.subject: gglearn timing-equalised login
says: pays the cost of a password hash for unknown or offboarded accounts
stops response time revealing which emails exist
protects against account enumeration by timing
cards.use: want to know why gglearn hashes a password even for unknown emails
not: returns faster for unknown emails to save server time

cards.subject: gglearn create-person action
says: takes a name, email, job role and initial password
creates an onboarding checklist for the new person
enrols the person in tracks recommended for their job role
cards.use: ask what happens when a gglearn manager adds a person
not: only sends the new person an email

cards.subject: gglearn onboarding checklist
says: includes shadowing a teammate on a real task
is created automatically when a person is added
mirrors an offboarding checklist at the other end of employment
cards.use: ask what gglearn creates for a new person
not: contains only payroll forms

cards.subject: gglearn offboarding checklist
says: asks for handover notes for each area the person owns
asks for answers to the ten questions only the person knows
includes returning equipment and revoking tool access
cards.use: ask what gglearn lists when a person leaves
not: lists only the leaver's holiday balance

cards.subject: gglearn handover note
says: is saved against the person who is leaving
can optionally be tied to a track
is added by a manager
cards.use: want to record knowledge in gglearn before someone departs
not: is generated automatically from the leaver's emails

cards.subject: Moksy staff-operations desk
says: is a named operating function that owns a queue and a bounded set of duties
is seated by people at levels
survives whoever sits at it
cards.use: ask how the Moksy staff-operations paper names a job
not: is a single named employee

cards.subject: Moksy unstaffed report
says: shows a desk with nobody seated as unstaffed
avoids showing the desk as an empty queue
makes a coverage gap visible
cards.use: want to know how the Moksy paper reports a desk with nobody at it
not: reports the desk as an empty queue

cards.subject: Moksy desk grouping
says: groups the proposed 32 desks by what they answer for
includes groups such as customer-facing, marketplace, money, trust and platform
ties each desk to a role in the existing workforce table
cards.use: ask how the Moksy paper organises its desks
not: puts all desks in a single list with no groups

cards.subject: Moksy duty class
says: labels a duty as make, decide, review or sign off
sits alongside a floor level and risk tags
describes the kind of action a duty involves
cards.use: ask how the Moksy paper categorises what a duty does
not: labels a duty by the colour of its queue

cards.subject: Moksy floor level
says: sets the minimum level a person needs to perform a duty
stops people below that level from being seated on the duty
is set for each duty rather than for each person
cards.use: ask what the lowest level for a duty is called in the Moksy paper
not: caps the highest level a person can reach

cards.subject: Moksy risk tag
says: marks duties involving money, personal data, irreversible actions or bulk actions
signals that senior or second-person approval is needed for high-risk duties
is attached to each duty
cards.use: ask how the Moksy paper flags dangerous duties
not: tags a duty with the desk's budget

cards.subject: Moksy operator-role set
says: contains four roles in the staff-operations paper
is mostly guarded by a single is-staff check
cannot distinguish a payouts clerk from a content editor
cards.use: ask why the Moksy paper says role checks are too coarse
not: is described as eight fine-grained desks in the paper

cards.subject: Moksy staff-operations status
says: is at founder review with nothing built
has case counts that are unverified until someone walks them
is a proposal to plan from, not evidence of coverage
cards.use: are asked whether the Moksy staff-operations design is live
not: is shipped and running in production

cards.subject: Moksy reviewer onboarding choices
says: asks the person to choose only what they do and at what level
works out everything else for the person to correct
follows the principle of easy, fast, automated and accurate
cards.use: ask what a new Moksy reviewer decides
not: asks the person to fill in a long form of ten choices

cards.subject: Moksy role-and-level grid
says: multiplies 25 roles by 8 levels to give 200 crosses
contains 148 real combinations
includes 52 combinations that are refused
cards.use: ask how many role-and-level combinations Moksy reviewer onboarding has
not: treats all 200 combinations as real

cards.subject: Moksy refused cross
says: rejects a role-and-level combination that does not exist
offers the nearest real level instead
is one of the 52 non-real combinations
cards.use: ask what happens when a reviewer picks an impossible role and level in Moksy
not: silently accepts the impossible combination

cards.subject: Moksy reviewer setup summary
says: shows title, setup minutes before the first deciding review, what the person may review, who reads their first reviews and how to ask for help
is shown for the person to correct
is worked out from the role and level
cards.use: ask what the Moksy reviewer onboarding shows after the two choices
not: hides all computed details from the person

qa.q: What is the main purpose of an onboarding checklist?
qa.right: To make sure every new hire gets the same complete start
wrong: To rank new hires against each other
To replace the manager's conversations with the new hire
To record why a person left
qa.why: A checklist gives consistency and a record of what has been done.

qa.q: What does least privilege mean?
qa.right: Each person gets only the access their job needs
wrong: Each person gets the access their seniority suggests
Only managers get any access
Access is granted once and never reviewed
qa.why: It limits the damage a mistaken or compromised account can do.

qa.q: When should access end for a person who leaves?
qa.right: When their employment ends, across every system
wrong: At the end of the month in which they leave
When they next try to sign in
After their manager notices unusual activity
qa.why: Delays leave an open door for no business reason.

qa.q: What is a buddy in onboarding?
qa.right: A peer named to help a newcomer with everyday questions
wrong: The person who decides the newcomer's pay
A senior leader who sponsors the newcomer's promotion
An external trainer who runs the induction
qa.why: A buddy is a friendly first contact, separate from the line manager.

qa.q: What is a one-to-one meeting for?
qa.right: A regular private conversation between a manager and a report about support, feedback and growth
wrong: A weekly status report to the whole team
A disciplinary hearing
A planning session for the next release
qa.why: It is the report's meeting as much as the manager's.

qa.q: Which of these is a handover note?
qa.right: A written record of what a person owns, how it works and what is pending
wrong: A farewell message to the team
A list of the leaver's holidays
A copy of the leaver's contract
qa.why: It lets a successor carry on without asking the leaver.

qa.q: What is a job description?
qa.right: A statement of the purpose, duties and requirements of a role
wrong: A record of how well someone did last year
A list of the company's open invoices
A summary of an interview
qa.why: It is the base from which a vacancy is advertised.

qa.q: Which describes annual leave?
qa.right: Planned paid time off requested in advance and approved against team cover
wrong: Time off taken at once when someone is ill
Time away that needs no notice
Time off available only after leaving the company
qa.why: Planning lets the team arrange cover.

qa.q: What are probation objectives?
qa.right: What the new hire must show by the end of the period, agreed at the start
wrong: The company's yearly revenue goals
The employee's preferred working hours
The criteria used to rank the whole team
qa.why: Clear, written objectives make the final decision fair.

qa.q: Why does a structured interview improve hiring?
qa.right: Every candidate gets the same questions scored against agreed criteria
wrong: Interviewers can follow their instincts about each person
The candidate controls the topics
It is shorter than any other format
qa.why: Comparable evidence reduces noise and bias.

qa.q: What does separation of duties require?
qa.right: That no single person can complete a risky task alone
wrong: That every task is done by the most senior person
That tasks are rotated monthly
That a person logs each action in a diary
qa.why: Requester and approver should differ.

qa.q: What is the difference between a mentor and a line manager?
qa.right: A mentor advises from outside the management chain and does not decide pay or promotion
wrong: A mentor sets the mentee's objectives
A mentor reviews performance for pay
A mentor must work in the same team
qa.why: Independence lets a mentee speak freely.

qa.q: What is a cover plan for an absence?
qa.right: An agreement before the absence naming who handles the work and decides in the person's place
wrong: A note written after the person returns
A request to the person to stay reachable on holiday
A list of the person's tasks given to the whole team
qa.why: Cover works only if planned before the absence.

qa.q: What does a retrospective produce?
qa.right: A few agreed improvement actions with owners
wrong: A plan of the next release
A list of the team's pay rises
A decision about who to promote
qa.why: It looks back at how the team worked, then picks changes.

qa.q: What does a competency matrix help with?
qa.right: Comparing a person's work with what each level expects
wrong: Scheduling meeting rooms
Recording leave balances
Choosing which tool to buy
qa.why: Observable descriptions make level expectations clear.

qa.q: Why is a shared account a problem for staff data?
qa.right: It makes it impossible to tell which person did an action
wrong: It is slower than individual accounts
It cannot hold more than one password
It requires a larger licence
qa.why: Individual accounts underpin logging and accountability.

qa.q: What is a role scorecard?
qa.right: A definition of the outcomes and competencies a hire must show, agreed before interviews
wrong: A ranking of candidates after interviews
A summary of salary bands
A list of questions to ask referees
qa.why: It makes ratings comparable across interviewers.

qa.q: What is recency bias in a performance review?
qa.right: Giving too much weight to the latest events in the period
wrong: Rating everyone the same
Letting one strong trait colour all scores
Preferring candidates from the same school
qa.why: Notes kept through the whole period reduce it.

qa.q: What does calibration do in a performance cycle?
qa.right: Compares ratings across managers so standards are consistent
wrong: Sets each person's salary
Lets each manager use a private scale
Replaces the one-to-one
qa.why: It is a discussion of evidence, not a vote.

qa.q: Why record a decision in a decision log?
qa.right: So later readers can see what was decided, by whom and why
wrong: So the decision cannot be changed under any circumstances
So meetings can be shorter
So the minutes can be shared outside the company
qa.why: The reasoning prevents repeated debates without new facts.

qa.q: What does data minimisation mean for an employee form?
qa.right: Ask only for the personal data needed for the stated purpose
wrong: Ask for everything in case it is useful
Hide the form from the employee
Store the answers in a spreadsheet
qa.why: Less data held means less to lose or misuse.

qa.q: What is a bus factor of one?
qa.right: Only one person holds the knowledge needed for the work
wrong: One vehicle is shared by the team
One person has too much work
One manager supervises everyone
qa.why: Cross-training and documentation raise it.

qa.q: What does gglearn do when it offboards a person?
qa.right: Marks them offboarded and bumps a session version so open sessions are signed out
wrong: Deletes the person's row
Waits for the cookie to expire
Emails the person a farewell
qa.why: The record stays, the access ends immediately.

qa.q: Who may a gglearn manager offboard?
qa.right: Only learners
wrong: Anyone
Only admins
Only themselves
qa.why: A review found a manager could lock out an admin, so it was fixed.

qa.q: In the Moksy staff-operations paper, what is a desk?
qa.right: A named operating function that owns a queue and duties and survives whoever sits at it
wrong: A physical workstation for one employee
A dashboard of reports
A customer's support ticket
qa.why: It makes a job a named thing instead of a habit.

qa.q: In Moksy reviewer onboarding, what does the person choose?
qa.right: What they do and at what level
wrong: Their salary and start date
Their desk and their manager
Their tools and their working hours
qa.why: Everything else is worked out and shown for correction.

qa.q: A new starter's first day is tomorrow and nothing is set up. What should you have done earlier?
qa.right: Pre-board: prepare accounts, equipment and a welcome after the offer is accepted
wrong: Wait until the first day to request access
Give them administrator access to save time
Ask them to set up their own accounts
qa.why: Pre-boarding removes idle time at the start.

qa.q: Your team lost its only person who knew the monthly payments process, and they have left. What is the best lesson to apply to the next similar role?
qa.right: Document processes, name a cover person and raise the bus factor before anyone leaves
wrong: Hire a replacement with the same name
Ask all staff to avoid leave
Keep processes verbal so they stay flexible
qa.why: Knowledge handover must begin before the last day.

qa.q: A leaver had the password to a shared account. Their personal login is disabled. What should you do next?
qa.right: Rotate the shared password and any keys they knew
wrong: Nothing, because their login is disabled
Ask the person to promise not to use it
Wait to see whether it is misused
qa.why: Disabling a login does not stop credentials that work independently.

qa.q: A manager approves their own expense claim in the system. Which principle is broken?
qa.right: Separation of duties
wrong: Data minimisation
Role-based learning paths
Pre-boarding
qa.why: The requester and approver must differ.

qa.q: A new hire has missed objectives for three weeks of a twelve-week probation. What should you do first?
qa.right: Hold an early conversation about the gap, support needed and what to change
wrong: Wait for the final review to tell them
Extend the probation without telling them
Move their objectives without recording it
qa.why: Early, specific feedback leaves time to improve and avoids surprises.

qa.q: Two managers rate similar work differently and one team has far higher ratings. What helps most?
qa.right: Calibration, comparing evidence across managers against the same standard
wrong: Giving the lenient manager's rating to everyone
Ranking people by who spoke up most
Letting each team keep its own scale
qa.why: Calibration reduces rater differences.

qa.q: An interview panel meets and the most senior person speaks first. What is the better way to run the debrief?
qa.right: Have every interviewer submit scores before discussion
wrong: Let the senior person state the decision, then discuss
Skip the debrief if the first round was positive
Choose the candidate most people remember
qa.why: Independent scoring stops anchoring on the loudest voice.

qa.q: A colleague cannot work because of illness and no one knows who covers their urgent tasks. What would have prevented this?
qa.right: An unplanned absence procedure and a cover plan known in advance
wrong: A stricter holiday policy
A longer probation period
A bigger meeting room
qa.why: People need to know whom to notify and who steps in.

qa.q: An employee wants to grow as a specialist and does not wish to manage others. What fits best?
qa.right: An individual contributor track with senior levels
wrong: Promotion into a management role regardless
Staying at the same level indefinitely
Moving to a different company
qa.why: Craft progression avoids forcing good practitioners into management.

qa.q: Many long-serving staff can open systems unrelated to their jobs. What is the problem and the fix?
qa.right: Permission creep, fixed by regular access reviews
wrong: Weak onboarding, fixed by longer orientation
Shared accounts, fixed by a new password
Poor calibration, fixed by 360 feedback
qa.why: Reviews compare held access to current duties.

qa.q: A privileged administrator is leaving. Who should check the offboarding steps?
qa.right: A second person, because privileged exits warrant a second pair of eyes
wrong: The leaver, since they know their access best
No one, to protect privacy
Any employee who asks
qa.why: This is separation of duties applied to exits.

qa.q: In an emergency the normal approver cannot be reached and a system must be fixed at once. What does an organisation use?
qa.right: Break-glass access that is logged and reviewed afterwards
wrong: Shared passwords left on a note
Permanent administrator rights for everyone
Waiting until the approver returns
qa.why: Emergency access is controlled and audited, not open-ended.

qa.q: A colleague says the 200 role-and-level crosses in Moksy reviewer onboarding are all valid. What is the correct response?
qa.right: 148 are real and 52 are refused with the nearest real level offered
wrong: All 200 are real
Only 25 are real
None are real until each person confirms
qa.why: The paper reports 25 roles by 8 levels giving 200 crosses.

qa.q: Someone says Moksy's staff-operations desks are already running. What should you check?
qa.right: The paper's own status: it is at founder review and nothing is built
wrong: The number of desks listed
Whether the desk names look professional
Whether the queue is empty
qa.why: A proposal is not evidence of coverage.

qa.q: Why does gglearn pay the cost of a password hash for unknown or offboarded accounts at login?
qa.right: So response time does not reveal which emails exist
wrong: To make logins slower for everyone
To log the user out later
To test the database speed
qa.why: Equal timing stops account enumeration.

qa.q: Why does gglearn re-read authorization from the database on every request?
qa.right: So role changes and offboarding take effect immediately
wrong: To reduce database load
Because cookies cannot be stored
To count page views
qa.why: It avoids waiting for a cookie to expire.

qa.q: A gglearn manager adds a person to the platform. What happens as a direct result?
qa.right: An onboarding checklist is created and the person is enrolled in tracks for their job role
wrong: The person is made an admin
Nothing until the person signs in
A leaving checklist is created
qa.why: Access, learning and people are set up together.

qa.q: Your company wants to know whether onboarding is working. Which measure is most direct?
qa.right: Time for a new hire to reach the expected level of work
wrong: Hours of training attended
Number of emails the new hire sent
Size of the welcome pack
qa.why: Time to productivity reflects real outcomes.

qa.q: An HR record export includes a colleague's health note and is to be sent to an outside adviser. What is the right approach?
qa.right: Share only what is needed, redact the rest and use an approved secure channel
wrong: Send the full file by group email
Post it on the team channel
Send it to the adviser's personal address
qa.why: Need-to-know and secure sharing apply to sensitive data.

qa.q: A manager repeatedly cancels the one-to-one with a struggling report. What is the likely effect?
qa.right: Problems stay hidden and the report feels unsupported
wrong: The report gains independence
The next review becomes more accurate
Feedback becomes more continuous
qa.why: The meeting is the place where support and feedback happen.

qa.q: A team repeats the same argument in meetings each month. Which practice addresses this?
qa.right: A decision log recording what was decided and why
wrong: A longer weekly meeting
A larger all-hands
A new job description
qa.why: The log stops debates being reopened without new facts.

qa.q: A candidate gives a strong first impression and an interviewer rates every criterion highly. Which bias is likely?
qa.right: Halo effect
wrong: Recency bias
Permission creep
Calibration
qa.why: One strong trait colours the rest.

qa.q: A growing team finds every task is called an ops job and no one knows who owns it. What does the desk idea suggest?
qa.right: Name the function, define its duties and queue and seat people at it
wrong: Hire more staff before defining anything
Give everyone every task
Rotate the work randomly each day
qa.why: Naming the job lets cover, training and handover happen.

qa.q: A candidate asks why a work sample is part of the hiring process. What is the best answer?
qa.right: It shows skill directly instead of only describing it
wrong: It replaces the interview
It measures personality
It is only required for managers
qa.why: Work samples give direct evidence of performance.

qa.q: What should be agreed between a manager and new hire in a 30-60-90 day plan?
qa.right: Expectations for learning, contributing and owning across the first three months
wrong: The new hire's pay for three years
The final probation outcome
Who will be promoted first
qa.why: It gives natural points for progress conversations.

qa.q: A leaver owned several customer relationships. What must the offboarding include?
qa.right: Transferring ownership and telling customers who their new contact is
wrong: Deleting the customer records
Leaving the accounts unassigned
Asking customers to wait for the leaver's replacement without notice
qa.why: Unowned customers are the main knowledge-loss risk.
